json.summary: A truck with a 'FELVESZEM' (I pick up) sign hits a pedestrian. The driver finds the injured man lying on his flatbed; the man explains he was hit on Gubacs Teréz road last Tuesday and both legs are broken. The driver denies it, gets exasperated, but eventually gives him a blanket because it is cold at night. The humour is deadpan absurdity: the truck's sign literally picked up the victim, who now lives on the flatbed, and the driver reluctantly accepts him.

characters.name: truck driver
characters.description: Long-haired, mustachioed man with a large nose, wearing a vest with pockets; appears in panels p1-p7. He owns/drives the truck and speaks in casual Budapest street slang with frequent strong swearing ('bazme', 'faszom', 'geci', 'kurva'). He denies the accident, gets frustrated, then accepts the injured man and gives him a blanket.

characters.name: injured man on flatbed
characters.description: The man with glasses, suit, and briefcase seen in p0 (the accident victim); after being hit, he lies on the truck's flatbed and speaks off-panel in later panels. He says he was hit on Gubacs Teréz road, both legs are broken, and it hurts/aches. He had two big shopping bags, which kept him from starving. His speech is colloquial, complaining, and somewhat old-fashioned/childish ('fájogat').

panels.description: A truck with a garbled company sign 'ÉPÖIPAI KITTELEZÉS • OG' on its cab and 'HLOTT!' / 'RITY!' on the cab windows. A man in a suit, glasses, and briefcase is walking/running away from the truck (or being hit from behind). A torch/lamp on a pole is attached to the cab. No speech bubbles.

The truck is seen from the flatbed side with sign '7722.683/FELVESZEM'. The long-haired truck driver stands on the right, hands on hips, looking at the truck. A speech bubble r1 'HRAHGHHRRR....' comes from the flatbed area, and the driver says r2 'MI A FASZOM?' (What the fuck?).

The driver asks r4 'KI VAGY...' (Who are you...). Two signs are on the truck side: r6 'FEKSZEM ITT.' and r7 '7722.683/FELVESZEM'. A speech bubble r5 from the flatbed explains the accident on Gubacs Teréz road. Tails: r4 points to the driver, r5 points to the flatbed.

The driver leans/reaches toward the truck and says r8 'NEM IS JÁRTAM ARRA MA...' (I haven't been there today...). The flatbed voice replies r9 'EZ MÚLT HÉT KEDDEN TÖRTÉNT...' (This happened last Tuesday...). Sign r11 '7722.683/FELVESZEM' is visible.

The driver says r12 'MÚLT HÉT KEDD? NE KAMUZZÁ! HOGY NEM HALTÁL ÉHEN?' (Last Tuesday? Don't bullshit! How didn't you starve?). The flatbed voice r13 explains he was coming out of the shop when hit, had two big bags. Sign r14 '7722·683/FELVESZEM'.
The driver walks away with a hand to his head, saying r15 'AKURVA ÉLET!' (For fuck's sake!). The truck sign r16 '7722 · 683/FELVESZEM' is visible. No speech from the victim.
The truck side is shown alone; a speech bubble r19 'AAAARRRGH....' comes from the flatbed. Sign r20 '7722 · 683/FELVESZEM'. The driver is absent.

The driver returns, points at the truck and says r21 'ITT EGY PLÉD, BAZME. ÉJJELENTE MÁR HIDEGEK VANNAK.' (Here's a blanket, fuck. It's cold at night.). Sign r22 '7722.683/FELVESZEM'. He is giving a blanket to the injured man.

notes: The central pun is the truck's sign 'FELVESZEM' ('I pick up'), which is a transport-service ad ('I'll pick you up') but also literally describes the truck picking up the pedestrian it hit onto its flatbed. The victim then lives on the flatbed; the driver eventually accepts him.

r0 'ÉPÖIPAI KITTELEZÉS • OG' is a garbled/misspelled company sign on the cab in p0. It is likely a background joke about unprofessional or nonsense signage. Keep it as a nonsense company name; it does not need to be translated word-for-word.

r3, r7, r11, r14, r16, r20, r22 all spell '7722.683/FELVESZEM' on the flatbed side. The punctuation changes (period, middle dot, spaces) across panels — a running gag of sloppy hand-lettering. The text means '7722.683 / I PICK UP' (phone number + service). Keep the digits and 'FELVESZEM'.
r6 'FEKSZEM ITT.' means 'I am lying here.' The injured man has put up this sign on the truck. It is a joke: he is advertising his presence on the flatbed. Keep as a sign.
r1 'HRAHGHHRRR....' and r19 'AAAARRRGH....' are groans of the injured man on the flatbed; not words, just pain sounds.
r2 'MI A FASZOM?' is vulgar Budapest slang: 'What the fuck?' (literally 'what [is] my dick?'). The driver uses strong casual swearing throughout.

r4: 'KI VAGY, ÉS MI A GECIT KERESEL A PLATÓMON, BAZME?' = 'Who are you, and what the fuck are you looking for on my flatbed, fuck?' 'geci' = semen, used as a vulgar intensifier; 'bazme' = clipped 'bazdmeg' = fuck. 'platómon' = 'on my flatbed' (from 'plató' flatbed + -m my + -on on); it may sound like 'Platón' (Plato) but is not a pun here.

r5: 'A GUBACS TERÉZ ÚTON ÜTÖTTEL, MINDKÉT LÁBAM ELTÖRÖTT, AZÓTA FÁJ. FÁJOGAT.' = 'You hit me on Gubacs Teréz road, both my legs are broken, since then it hurts. It aches.' Gubacs Teréz út is a real Budapest street name. 'Fájogat' is colloquial/nonstandard for 'it keeps hurting/aching', sounding childish or rural; keep the repetition 'fáj. fájogat.'
r8: 'NEM IS JÁRTAM ARRA MA, BAZME... A KÖZELBE SE.' = 'I haven't even been there today, fuck... not even close.' The driver denies being on Gubacs Teréz road.
r9: 'EZ MÚLT HÉT KEDDEN TÖRTÉNT...' = 'This happened last Tuesday...' The victim corrects the timeline.

r12: 'MÚLT HÉT KEDD? NE KAMUZZÁ! HOGY NEM HALTÁL ÉHEN?' = 'Last Tuesday? Don't bullshit! How didn't you starve to death?' 'kamuzzá' = 'kamuzzál' (don't bullshit); 'haltál éhen' = you starved/died of hunger. The punchline: if he has been lying on the flatbed since last Tuesday, he should have starved.

r13: 'KIFELÉ JÖTTEM A BOLTBÓL, AMIKOR TELIBE KAPOTT... KÉT NAGY SZATYOR...' = 'I was coming out of the shop when [it] hit me full-on... two big bags...' 'telibe kapott' = got hit full-on; 'szatyor' = shopping bag. He survived because he had two big bags of groceries. This resolves the starvation question.
r15: 'AKURVA ÉLET!' = 'A kurva élet!' = 'The fucking life!' / 'For fuck's sake!' Written as one word for emphasis. Driver's frustration.

r21: 'ITT EGY PLÉD, BAZME. ÉJJELENTE MÁR HIDEGEK VANNAK.' = 'Here's a blanket, fuck. It's already cold at night.' 'éjjelente' = at night (slightly folksy/literary); 'hidegek vannak' = colloquial 'it's cold'. The driver has accepted the victim and now cares for him.

Background cab window lettering in p0: 'HLOTT!' and 'RITY!' — not in an editable red box, nonsensical/background. It may be garbled signage or graffiti. Keep as background decoration; no translation needed.

The man in p0 with glasses, suit, and briefcase is the victim before/at the moment of the accident. He does not speak in p0; his later off-panel voice (r1, r5, r9, r13, r19) comes from the flatbed. The truck driver (long-haired man in vest) is a separate character.

Running gag: the flatbed sign's punctuation changes across panels (r3, r7, r11, r14, r16, r20, r22). It is the same text '7722.683/FELVESZEM' but with inconsistent periods/middle dots/spaces. Translators should keep the inconsistency if possible or note it as sloppy hand-lettering.

Cultural reference: 'Gubacs Teréz út' is a Budapest street; for non-Hungarian audiences it can be kept as a proper name. 'Plató' is a flatbed truck; the joke hinges on 'felveszem' (pick up) being both a service ad and the literal action of the truck picking up the hit pedestrian.

Verbal tic: the driver repeatedly uses 'bazme' (r4, r8, r21) and other vulgarities. Translate with a consistent level of strong but casual swearing (e.g. 'fuck', 'damn'). The victim's speech is more complaining and old-fashioned ('fájogat').
The truck's 'FELVESZEM' sign has phone number '7722.683'. In Hungarian phone numbers, this is a seven-digit number (or 772-2683). It should be kept as digits.
No proper names are given; use 'truck driver' and 'injured man on flatbed' consistently.
